prompt:
Analyze the following external review feedback and check how it was addressed.
You have tools available — use `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- ':(exclude).planwerk'` to see ALL changes on this feature branch. You can also read individual files.

Generate a JSON object with:
- "resolution_summary": A concise summary (2-4 sentences) of what was done overall to address the review.
- "comment_resolutions": An array of strings, one per code comment (in the same order), each describing what was changed at that location. If there are no code comments, return an empty array.

IMPORTANT: If changes were made to files or locations NOT directly mentioned in the review feedback, the resolution_summary MUST explicitly list these additional changes and explain WHY they were necessary (e.g., 'Applied new pattern X from reviewer comment to N additional matching locations: [list files]'). This makes broad changes traceable to the original review comment.

## Review Feedback


## Inline Code Comments
[0] internal/common/job/job.go:157: **`normalizePodSpecDefaults` is incomplete — missing pod-level API-server defaults**

`normalizeContainerDefaults` correctly fills in `ImagePullPolicy`, `TerminationMessagePath`, and `TerminationMessagePolicy`. However, the Kubernetes API server also applies pod-level defaults that are not covered here:

| Field | API-server default |
|---|---|
| `ServiceAccountName` | `"default"` |
| `DNSPolicy` | `"ClusterFirst"` |
| `SchedulerName` | `"default-scheduler"` |
| `TerminationGracePeriodSeconds` | `30` |
| `EnableServiceLinks` | `true` |

When a caller constructs a Job with these fields at their zero values (which is almost always), the stored spec will have `ServiceAccountName: "default"` while `desiredSpec.ServiceAccountName == ""`. `apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual` (backed by `reflect.DeepEqual` for string fields) returns `false`, so `RunJob` will delete and recreate the completed Job on every reconcile — exactly the behaviour `normalizePodSpecDefaults` was designed to prevent.

The unit tests do not catch this because the fake client does not apply API-server defaulting. In a real cluster, `db_sync` would re-run on every reconcile cycle after completing successfully.

The fix is to also normalize the common pod-level defaults:

```go
func normalizePodSpecDefaults(spec *corev1.PodSpec) {
    normalizeContainerDefaults(spec.Containers)
    normalizeContainerDefaults(spec.InitContainers)

    // Pod-level API-server defaults
    if spec.ServiceAccountName == "" {
        spec.ServiceAccountName = "default"
    }
    if spec.DNSPolicy == "" {
        spec.DNSPolicy = corev1.DNSClusterFirst
    }
    if spec.SchedulerName == "" {
        spec.SchedulerName = "default-scheduler"
    }
    if spec.TerminationGracePeriodSeconds == nil {
        defaultGrace := int64(30)
        spec.TerminationGracePeriodSeconds = &defaultGrace
    }
    if spec.EnableServiceLinks == nil {
        t := true
        spec.EnableServiceLinks = &t
    }
}
```

A corresponding test using the fake client with these pod-level fields pre-populated (simulating API-server storage) would make the fix verifiable without envtest.

[1] internal/common/deployment/deployment.go:52: **API-server pod-level defaults cause an infinite spec-update loop**

`apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual(existing.Spec, deploy.Spec)` compares the full `DeploymentSpec`, including the pod template's `PodSpec`. When a caller constructs a `Deployment` without setting `ServiceAccountName`, `DNSPolicy`, `SchedulerName`, `TerminationGracePeriodSeconds`, or `EnableServiceLinks`, the API server writes the defaults into `existing.Spec.Template.Spec`, while `deploy.Spec.Template.Spec` retains the zero values. Because `apiequality.Semantic` uses `reflect.DeepEqual` for plain string and integer fields, `""` ≠ `"default"` and `nil` ≠ `&30`, so the guard is **always false** in production.

Consequences:
1. `c.Update` is called on every reconcile even when nothing actually changed.
2. The API server increments `Generation` on each update.
3. `IsDeploymentReady` returns `false` while `ObservedGeneration` lags, so the reconciler never sees a stable `ready=true` signal.
4. This is an infinite update loop: the deployment controller reacts to the spec-update, the operator reconciles again, detects the (spurious) diff, and updates again.

Unit tests miss this because the fake client does not apply API-server pod-spec defaulting.

The most robust fix is to normalize the pod-level defaults on `deploy.Spec.Template.Spec` before the comparison (analogous to `normalizePodSpecDefaults` in `job.go`), or to apply `controllerutil.CreateOrUpdate` which uses a server-side PATCH and avoids the object-level diff entirely.

[2] internal/common/job/job.go:108: **`EnsureCronJob` spec comparison is sensitive to API-server pod-level defaults**

`apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual(existing.Spec, cronJob.Spec)` compares the full `CronJobSpec`, which includes `JobTemplate.Spec.Template.Spec`. The same API-server pod-level defaulting issue that affects `EnsureDeployment` applies here: callers that leave `ServiceAccountName`, `DNSPolicy`, `SchedulerName`, `TerminationGracePeriodSeconds`, or `EnableServiceLinks` at their zero values will produce a stored spec that differs from the desired spec on every reconcile.

The consequence is `c.Update` being called on every reconcile — continuous unnecessary churn on the CronJob resource and spurious watch events. Unlike `RunJob`, this does not delete-recreate, but it still causes the CronJob controller to reprocess the CronJob on every operator reconcile cycle.
